Beginning as Craig Patrickâs right-hand man on the personnel side his first year, before spending the next two seasons behind the bench, the Penguins went Stanley Cup champs-Stanley Cup champs Presidentsâ Trophy winner in Bowmanâs three years with the team.  
Bowman was at his coaching best in the opening two rounds of the â92 playoffs. His mid-series shift to a neutral-zone trap led a 3-1 first-round series comeback against Washington. In the next round, the Penguins overcame Mario Lemieuxâs broken hand to erase a 2-1 series deficit against the NHLâs best team, the New York Rangers.

Pittsburgh went on to conclude the â92 postseason with an NHL-record 11-game win streak. (Bowmanâs Penguins won 14-straight playoff games between â92 and â93, the NHLâs longest overall win streak over multiple seasons).  
Although the â92-93 Penguins fell short of a three-peat, Bowmanâs club is still the Penguinsâ most accomplished regular-season team. In the midst of winning the Penguins only Presidentsâ Trophy, that club set team marks for wins (56), points (119), and goals for (367), and it established a 17-game win streak thatâs still the NHL record.
